hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Danville, CA from a Third-Generation Builder
hero.subheadline: Chris Gayler leads the design-build firm his grandfather founded in 1961. Designers, project managers and carpenters work under one roof, and every project gets a fixed-cost budget before construction starts.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling by a Danville, CA design-build firm: contemporary Lafayette kitchen with light oak flat-panel cabinets and a long island

intro.h2: A family process built to hit the date and the number
paragraphs: Kitchen remodeling in Danville, CA has been the Gayler family's trade for more than six decades. George Gayler took over his father's firm in 1980 and built the Gayler Process, a design-build system that links design and construction so nothing gets lost between the two. His son Chris runs it today from a showroom on Hartz Way.

The firm says every project has been delivered on time and on budget since 1999. That starts with a fixed-cost budget estimate and a design you approve in 3D before work begins. After the last walkthrough, a 5-year workmanship warranty and scheduled check-ins keep the team in touch.

about.h2: Chris Gayler, third generation at the helm
about.text: Chris Gayler's grandfather founded the company in 1961. His father George took it over in 1980, a year after earning his contractor's license, and grew it with Chris's mother Darlene, who joined in 2000. Chris has worked in the business since 2003 and took over in January 2020. A UC Santa Barbara graduate, he brings his own contractor's license, a communications degree and a tech background. He serves on the boards of the San Ramon Rotary and the Valley Education Foundation. His goal, in his words, is to leave things in even better shape than he found them.

image.alt: Chris Gayler and his father George Gayler reviewing floor plans

process.h2: How a Gayler kitchen comes together

steps.title: A phone call
steps.text: You share your vision, the team answers questions and explains the design-build steps. If it looks like a good fit, an in-home visit is scheduled.

steps.title: In-home consultation
steps.text: The team walks your space, reviews the current layout, talks cabinetry, countertops, lighting and flooring, and takes precise measurements and photos.

steps.title: Concept and preliminary estimate
steps.text: After you sign a design agreement and fill out a design questionnaire, the designers prepare a conceptual floor plan, a preliminary estimate and a clear scope of work.

steps.title: Final design in 3D
steps.text: You see a 3D rendering, choose finishes with the interior designer and receive the final construction estimate before signing the construction agreement.

steps.title: Build, clean and walk through
steps.text: A dedicated project manager runs the job with 24/7 online schedule access, the site is cleaned daily, and a final walkthrough checklist closes it out.

service_area.h2: Serving the Tri-Valley and Lamorinda from Hartz Way
service_area.text: The office and showroom sit at 825 Hartz Way in Danville, open Monday through Friday. From there, Gayler works across the Tri-Valley and Lamorinda: Alamo, Diablo and San Ramon close to home, Pleasanton, Dublin and Livermore to the south and east, and Walnut Creek, Lafayette, Orinda and Moraga over the hill. Recent jobs include an ADU in Alamo, a kitchen addition in San Ramon and a whole-home remodel in Danville.

faq.h2: Before you call: common Danville remodeling questions

items.a: Gayler backs its workmanship for five years, which it describes as five times the one-year industry standard, and schedules follow-ups after you move back in. At the final walkthrough you also get a binder holding the manufacturer warranties for every product used, from cabinets and countertops to backsplash and flooring.

items.q: Can you plan a kitchen or bath for aging in place?
items.a: Yes. Accessibility and aging in place are among the most common requests the design team hears. A recent Danville primary bathroom was built around them, with a curbless shower, grab bars and a fold-down seat. Universal design can be part of any bathroom or kitchen plan.

items.q: Can we stay in the house during the remodel?
items.a: Often, yes. One San Ramon couple wrote that they lived and worked at home through their 12-plus-week primary bathroom remodel, and that the crew left the house clean and safe every day. The team cleans the job site at the end of each workday to keep disruption down.

items.q: How will I know where my project stands?
items.a: Every project is assigned a dedicated project manager, and you get real-time, 24/7 access to your schedule and project details through the firm's online scheduling software. Changes to the original plan and timeline are shared as they happen, so you are not left guessing.

items.q: How do you keep a remodel on budget?
items.a: Gayler builds the design and the estimate together. You get a preliminary estimate with the concept plan, then a final construction estimate once finishes are chosen, before you sign. For additions, conceptual drawings come with a cost versus budget analysis so you can adjust scope early.

final_cta.h2: Talk kitchens with a Gayler designer
final_cta.text: Call the Danville office, open weekdays 8 am to 4 pm, or request a personal in-home consultation.
